From Hotel: 🚕 6 min → Cape Cod Maritime Museum
1. Cape Cod Maritime Museum
Waterfront museum in Hyannis displaying maritime history, ship models, whaling artifacts, and trade-vessel exhibits spanning three centuries of the region's seafaring past. The boat-building program runs year-round alongside seasonal exhibitions.

2. Sandwich Glass Museum
Sandwich was home to the first successful pressed-glass operation in the United States, founded in 1825 by Deming Jarves. The museum displays over 5,000 pieces from the Boston and Sandwich Glass Company, with working glassblowing demonstrations covering blown, molded, and pressed glass techniques.

3. Heritage Museums and Gardens
100-acre estate museum in Sandwich featuring American art, a vintage automobile collection, and one of the largest rhododendron gardens in the United States. A 1912 carousel, replica Shaker Round Barn, and historic windmill occupy grounds that bloom brilliantly in late spring.

1. Eastham Windmill
Built around 1680, this is the oldest windmill on the peninsula and among the oldest still standing in the United States. The restored Dutch-style smock mill sits on the Eastham Town Green and opens for self-guided tours in summer.

Massachusetts Audubon Society sanctuary protecting 1,000 acres of marshes, pine forests, and tidal flats on the Outer Cape. Walking trails lead to a salt marsh observation deck; globally significant shorebird stopover site during Atlantic flyway migration.

High oceanfront bluffs frame the beach marking Guglielmo Marconi's 1903 transatlantic wireless telegraph site. Wide sandy beach with dramatic cliff views; the original antenna footprints are marked at the overlook above.

1. Cape Cod Museum of Natural History
Regional natural history museum in Brewster tracing the Cape's geology, wildlife, and Native American heritage through rotating exhibitions and living exhibits. A salt-marsh boardwalk trail behind the building leads to Stony Brook Valley. Freshwater aquariums and Bird Alley of mounted specimens anchor the permanent collection.

2. Nickerson State Park
Massachusetts state park in Brewster protecting 1,967 acres of former estate land centered on eight kettle ponds carved by glaciers. Cliff Pond and Flax Pond are the most popular swimming sites; 8.5 miles of bike trails and 10 miles of hiking trails loop through pitch-pine and oak forest.

Day 5
From Hotel: 🚕 1h → Pilgrim Monument
1. Pilgrim Monument
The 252-foot granite tower in Provincetown, completed in 1910, is the tallest all-granite structure in the United States. Built to mark where the Mayflower Compact was signed in 1620, visitors climb 60 ramps and 116 stairs to panoramic views of Cape Cod Bay and the Atlantic. The museum below traces the Pilgrims' first landing.
📖 Read more

⏰ ~1 hr 30 min
⚠️ Closed January and February
📍 1 High Pole Hill Road · Provincetown
🚶 26 min · 🚕 2 min → Provincetown Art Association and Museum
2. Provincetown Art Association and Museum
Founded in 1914 at 460 Commercial Street, PAAM preserves over a century of Cape Cod artistic heritage. The permanent collection spans Provincetown masters including Charles Hawthorne, Hans Hofmann, and Robert Motherwell; six gallery spaces host rotating exhibitions year-round alongside the permanent collection.
📖 Read more

3. Herring Cove Beach
Wide crescent beach on the western tip of the peninsula facing the bay, celebrated for spectacular sunsets. Warm sheltered bay waters make it the calmest swimming beach on the Outer Cape.
📖 Read more
🏛️ Open 24/7

📍 Province Lands Road · Provincetown
🚕 14 min → Highland Light
4. Highland Light
Established in 1797 and rebuilt in brick in 1857, Highland Light is the oldest lighthouse on Cape Cod and stands 170 feet above the Atlantic on clay cliffs in Truro. Moved 450 feet inland in 1996 as erosion approached the base, the lantern remains active as a Coast Guard aid to navigation; guided climbs reach the top for panoramic views.
📖 Read more

⏰ ~1 hr
⚠️ Open May through October only

🍮 Local Tastes
Lobster Roll
The peninsula's signature dish — cold mayo-dressed or warm butter-drizzled lobster meat in a toasted split-top bun. Every fish house on the peninsula serves a version; Captain Frosty's in Dennis is the most-cited local benchmark.
📍 Fish houses across the peninsula
New England Clam Chowder
Thick cream-based chowder loaded with quahog clams, potatoes, and salt pork. The local version is noticeably chunkier and saltier than Boston's — best sampled at Chatham Fish and Lobster Co. on the Fish Pier.
📍 Fish Pier · Chatham
Wellfleet Oysters
Wellfleet's cold, nutrient-rich tidal flats produce oysters considered among the finest on the East Coast — briny, plump, and with a distinctive mineral finish. Freshest served raw at Mac's Seafood in Wellfleet Harbor.
📍 Shellfish Harbor · Wellfleet

📡 The First Transatlantic Radio Message Was Sent From a Cliff That No Longer Exists

In January 1903, President Theodore Roosevelt sent a greeting in Morse code from a station on these bluffs to King Edward VII in England — the first transatlantic wireless message ever transmitted, tapped out from four 210-foot towers standing where the Marconi Beach overlook is today. Marconi's own engineers knew almost immediately that the site had a problem: by 1906 the sea cliff was eroding roughly three feet a year, and the front towers were already at risk of toppling onto the beach below. The station was dismantled and abandoned by 1920, and the ocean has since taken most of the original site outright — the ground the towers stood on has largely eroded into the Atlantic, leaving only markers on the bluff where a piece of communications history briefly existed.

The Pilgrims never actually landed at Plymouth first. The Mayflower dropped anchor in Provincetown Harbor, at the very tip of the Cape near where Herring Cove Beach sits today, and it was here — not at Plymouth Rock — that 41 passengers signed the Mayflower Compact establishing self-government before anyone had gone ashore to settle. Only after determining the harbor wasn't suitable for a permanent colony did the ship continue on to Plymouth. The famous founding document of the Plymouth Colony was written and signed on Cape Cod.
